lines.text: It takes the smithy a month of failures that crack the yard stones, and then one morning it doesn't fail. On the wall above the gate sits an iron throat on a timber carriage, pointed west.
Half the town turns out for the first shot. The powder speaks once, and across the valley the old dead oak comes apart.
Dad made horseshoes his whole life. I made a cannon. Don't tell him.
Nobody says the word war. Everybody thinks it. The town has teeth now, and a direction to point them.
